tagline: Bolivia's whitewashed constitutional capital is a UNESCO colonial jewel where independence was declared, dinosaur footprints climb a cliff and the altitude is mercifully kind.
overview: Sucre is where Bolivia became Bolivia: independence was declared in 1825 in the Casa de la Libertad. Named for revolutionary Antonio José de Sucre, the city of whitewashed buildings and red tile roofs is the country's constitutional capital — though the government sits in La Paz.

The whole colonial centre is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, built with silver wealth from nearby Potosí. The cathedral towers over Plaza 25 de Mayo, convents hide quiet courtyards, and the markets sell weavings from the surrounding Quechua villages.

On the city edge, the Cal Orck'o cliff displays over 5,000 dinosaur footprints tilting up a cement quarry wall — the largest collection of tracks ever found. Sucre's gentle 2,800-metre altitude and springlike climate make it Bolivia's favourite place to linger and learn Spanish.

funFacts.title: WHERE BOLIVIA WAS BORN
funFacts.text: Independence was proclaimed at the Casa de la Libertad in 1825.

funFacts.title: THE WHITE CITY
funFacts.text: Colonial law required buildings to be whitewashed — the tradition that earned the nickname survives today.

funFacts.title: TWO CAPITALS
funFacts.text: Sucre is the constitutional capital; La Paz holds the government. Bolivia refuses to choose.

funFacts.title: A WALL OF DINOSAUR TRACKS
funFacts.text: Cal Orck'o's near-vertical cliff shows over 5,000 footprints from at least 8 dinosaur species.

funFacts.title: SILVER PAID FOR IT
funFacts.text: Sucre's churches and convents were built with fortunes from Potosí's silver mountain.

funFacts.title: A GENTLE ALTITUDE
funFacts.text: At 2,810 metres, Sucre is kinder to visitors than La Paz — and the climate is famously mild.

funFacts.title: THE TEXTILE MARKETS
funFacts.text: Tarabuco's Sunday market brings weavers in traditional dress from mountain villages.

funFacts.title: A CASTLE THAT ISN'T
funFacts.text: The pink Castillo de la Glorieta was a prince's folly, mixing architectural styles freely.

funFacts.title: STUDENT CITY
funFacts.text: Sucre's university, founded in 1624, is one of the oldest in the Americas.

funFacts.title: HOME OF THE NEW BOLIVIANO
funFacts.text: The capital prints its money? No — but the coin and currency museum explains Bolivia's minting history.
